description:
Commerce Wars
v0.2.0 - late-game market and military pressure - for Starsector 0.98a

Success paints a target. You out-produce the Persean League on heavy machinery, undercut Sindria's fuel monopoly, flood the Church's food markets - and your intel screen fills with grievances. First diplomatic notes. Then ultimatums. Then enforcement fleets.

Commerce Wars is a standalone, vanilla-only mod that gives the sector's factions a reason to push back against a dominant player polity - economically motivated, militarily grounded, and generic: any faction whose export business you muscle in on develops a grievance. Your military buildup draws the same attention.

Download

CommerceWars-0.2.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save. LunaLib optional (full in-game config menu).

How grievances work
Every week the mod recomputes sector export market shares - the same numbers you see on the commodity info screens. A faction develops a grievance over a commodity when it is a significant producer and your share rivals theirs. Each aggrieved faction gets a colony-crisis-style intel screen: a resentment bar from 0 to 600, with a diplomatic warning at 200, a formal ultimatum at 400, and enforcement fleets at 600. Per-commodity monthly factors show exactly why they are angry.

Compliance detection is automatic. The demand is "get your share down" - how is your business. Downgrade the industry, demolish it, lose the share to a rival, or bomb your own customer base; the vanilla economy recomputes and the dispute cools on its own.

Your options at the ultimatum:

Comply - lose the contested share, the grievance decays away
Settle - one-off payments buy down accumulated resentment, priced off your contested export income (a coalition must be paid as a bloc)
Commission - a military grievance is laid to rest while your arsenal flies their flag (resigning is not forgotten)
Defy - fight what comes

Enforcement - grounded, adaptive, multi-front

Strike fleets are sized to overmatch your actual defenses, but hard capped by the faction's real military-industrial capacity: bases, stations, war industry. No magic fleets - disrupting their war industry genuinely shrinks what they can send at you.

Adaptive payloads: each fleet decides in real time. Standing defenses too strong to storm? Shell them open first. Then disrupt the industries behind the grievance, one landing at a time - falling back to bombardment or stockpile raids when nothing worth raiding remains. Every raid intel carries a fleet-by-fleet operations report.
Coalitions strike on multiple fronts: factions too weak to press demands alone pool behind a leader. Their joint strike launches one raid per member, under its own flag, against the colony that most offends its own grievance - and arrivals are synchronized, so you cannot repel them piecemeal with one fleet and a repair dock.
Sabotage window: every strike opens with a planning phase at its staging market. Knock out that market's military base or high command in time and the contingent aborts outright.
Item heists: at high escalation an oversized contingent storms the vault for an installed nanoforge or synchrotron while its partners raid diversionary fronts. Lifting an asset takes an overwhelming ground advantage - and stolen items are installed on their own markets, where a raid of yours can take them back.
Ground truth: raiders only take or disrupt what they can actually reach - the same raid-strength-vs-defender-strength math the player's own raids face, planetary shield and garrison marines included.

The strength gate - and earned silence

Factions only press demands while militarily on par with you or superior. Military score is functional military infrastructure only: patrol commands, bases, high commands, battlestations, war industry. A sprawl of garrisonless trade ports projects no force.

Too weak alone, aggrieved factions form a coalition behind a single leader - and the pooled strength is what makes the ultimatum credible. Break it: defeat their joint strike and partners can wash their hands of the alliance, demoralized out of coalition politics with their own resentment vented. Outgrow every plausible coalition and the demands simply stop. Earned silence.

Counterplay ladder

Defeat the strike fleets (their bar resets - but each defeat escalates the next attempt)
Abort strikes at the source during the planning window
Tac-bomb their competing production or their war industry
Settle, comply, or take a commission
Sat-bomb the competitor into the ground - at vanilla atrocity prices, and the victim's grievance becomes a permanent vendetta: no settlements, no truces, saturation bombardment in return, ending only when one side has no worlds left

Your own raids and bombardments against an aggrieved faction spike its resentment instantly - and a big enough spike triggers enforcement on the spot.

Total War (config, off by default): strips story-critical protection from every market. Any world can be bombed down and destroyed; factions can be entirely eliminated. Questlines anchored on destroyed worlds will strand - you were warned.

Compatibility and config

Vanilla API only; no hard dependencies. LunaLib optional for the in-game config menu (detection thresholds, accrual rates, strike scaling, coalition behavior, vendetta, Total War, debug tools).
Safe to add to an existing save. Removing mid-save is not supported.
Defers to vanilla colony crises: a faction whose vanilla crisis is active speaks through that instead of double-dipping.

Source: github.com/pogoman/CommerceWars

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, vanilla-only, safe to add mid-save — designed to stack.

Threat Incursion (v0.2.0) — the swarm colonizes the sector and raids the core worlds. Disrupt their supplies chains and steal their fabrication cores.
Commerce Wars (v0.2.0) — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked (v0.1.0) — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution (v0.3.1) — a late-game colony crisis: prosper too hard and the Remnant come to collect.
Useful Planetary Shield (v0.1.2) — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

Disclaimer: This post and these mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.

aiDescription: Factions develop grievances when your export share rivals theirs or your military buildup threatens them, escalating from diplomatic warnings to ultimatums and enforcement fleets. You can comply, settle with payments, commission their military, or defy them and fight adaptive strike fleets that target your industries and defenses. Coalitions form when factions are too weak alone, and total war mode removes story protections to allow complete faction elimination.
